Two men came down the lane at dusk, and a third sat on the gate with his boots swinging above the ditch. The carter knelt in the mud beside the near wheel, working the loose spoke free with a short hammer, and swore at it under his breath. Eight riders waited at the turn of the road, two of them dismounted and holding their horses by the bridle. The old lamp on the post had been lit early, though the sky was still green over the roofs, and a dog lay across the step of the inn with its chin on its paws. Nobody spoke for a long while. Then the taller of the two men took off his hat, wiped the band with his sleeve, and walked on toward the lamp.
